status: Research candidates; valuation, weights and broker availability pending
methodology: Primary company releases, SEC holdings filings and ETF issuer documents. Strategy fit and risks are AGI research judgments, not statements by Vested. This is a curated shortlist, not an exhaustive quantitative screen. No target prices or return forecasts have been calculated. Existing portfolio allocations are unchanged.

TXG.name: 10x Genomics
TXG.fit: Single-cell and spatial research tools diversify a therapeutics-heavy genomics basket.
TXG.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $151m; excluding litigation settlements, underlying revenue grew 3%.
TXG.risk: Research-budget sensitivity and weak underlying growth; settlement revenue distorts comparisons.
TXG.reviewGate: Check recurring consumables growth, instrument utilisation, cash burn and valuation excluding settlements.

PACB.name: Pacific Biosciences
PACB.fit: Long-read sequencing tools provide a different technology exposure.
PACB.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $39.0m versus $39.8m a year earlier; 2026 guidance was $155–165m.
PACB.risk: Speculative: continuing losses, funding/dilution risk and competition.
PACB.reviewGate: Require a funded runway and evidence of installed-base utilisation before considering any allocation.

NTSK.name: Netskope
NTSK.fit: Cloud and network security extends coverage beyond endpoint protection.
NTSK.evidence: September 2 FY2027 Q2 announcement reported ARR of $899m, up 27%, and revenue of $221m, up 29%.
NTSK.risk: Crowded security market; growth does not establish GAAP profitability or an attractive price.
NTSK.reviewGate: Reconcile cash flow, stock compensation, retention and enterprise value/recurring revenue.

FFIV.name: F5
FFIV.fit: Application delivery and application security add a different security workload.
FFIV.evidence: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $865m, up 11%; product revenue grew 19%.
FFIV.risk: Hardware refresh cycles and broader networking exposure make this less pure cybersecurity.
FFIV.reviewGate: Separate recurring security/software growth from cyclical hardware demand.

ANET.name: Arista Networks
ANET.fit: High-speed networking supports AI clusters and cloud infrastructure.
ANET.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $3.036bn, up 37.7%; GAAP operating margin was 45.4%.
ANET.risk: Large-customer concentration and dependence on hyperscaler capital expenditure.
ANET.reviewGate: Value normalised earnings under slower customer spending; check overlap with chip and cloud holdings.

VRT.name: Vertiv
VRT.fit: Power and cooling provide physical AI infrastructure exposure.
VRT.evidence: Q2 2026 sales were $3.274bn, up 24%, including 18% organic growth.
VRT.risk: Capacity execution, order cancellation and a reversal in data-centre spending.
VRT.reviewGate: Test cash conversion and backlog quality; do not extrapolate peak growth into valuation.

ORCL.name: Oracle
ORCL.fit: Cloud infrastructure plus enterprise software adds another major platform.
ORCL.evidence: FY2027 Q1 revenue was $19.3bn, up 30%; cloud infrastructure revenue was $7.4bn, up 121%.
ORCL.risk: Large infrastructure commitments, funding needs and customer concentration; bookings are not earned revenue.
ORCL.reviewGate: Reconcile capital expenditure, debt, free cash flow and contracted returns before pricing the growth.

EQIX.name: Equinix
EQIX.fit: Data centres and interconnection broaden a software-heavy cloud basket.
EQIX.evidence: Q2 2026 recurring revenue grew 11%; annualised gross bookings grew 23%, with 9,700 net new interconnections.
EQIX.risk: Interest rates, construction costs and power availability; REIT metrics differ from software metrics.
EQIX.reviewGate: Use AFFO per share, leverage and development returns rather than software revenue multiples.

PWR.name: Quanta Services
PWR.fit: Grid construction and electrical infrastructure fit electrification and domestic investment.
PWR.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $9.56bn versus $6.77bn; backlog reached $53.4bn.
PWR.risk: Labour shortages, acquisitions and project execution; not all revenue is renewable energy.
PWR.reviewGate: Disaggregate organic growth and acquisitions; review backlog margins and cash conversion.

EMR.name: Emerson Electric
EMR.fit: Industrial automation is a route to manufacturing productivity and reshoring exposure.
EMR.evidence: Fiscal Q3 2026 sales rose 7%, underlying sales 6%, and orders 7%.
EMR.risk: Industrial investment cycles and integration risk; global operations dilute a pure US reshoring thesis.
EMR.reviewGate: Verify geographic revenue and automation exposure; compare normalised cash yield with industrial peers.

BHP.name: BHP Group
BHP.fit: Diversified copper exposure offers an alternative to smaller single-commodity miners.
BHP.evidence: FY2026 copper production was about 2m tonnes; copper contributed over half of underlying EBITDA.
BHP.risk: Iron ore and China exposure remain substantial; commodity prices and project costs can reverse.
BHP.reviewGate: Value assets on mid-cycle commodity prices, not current spot margins; verify ADR availability.

RIO.name: Rio Tinto
RIO.fit: Copper and lithium projects broaden critical-material exposure.
RIO.evidence: The 2026 half-year presentation identifies growth investment in copper and lithium and capex up to $11bn in 2026/27.
RIO.risk: Iron ore concentration, project execution and lithium price volatility.
RIO.reviewGate: Measure actual segment exposure and project economics; verify the US ADR rather than another listing.

GEV.name: GE Vernova
GEV.fit: Grid equipment fits energy infrastructure; nuclear technology is an additional, indirect exposure.
GEV.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $11.1bn, up 22% reported and 12% organically. The company also reports GE Vernova Hitachi nuclear projects.
GEV.risk: Diversified gas, wind and grid business: neither a pure renewable nor a pure nuclear company.
GEV.reviewGate: Review segment profitability and nuclear revenue materiality; stress order conversion and cash advances.

ABT.name: Abbott Laboratories
ABT.fit: Diagnostics and medical devices broaden exposure to ageing-related healthcare demand.
ABT.evidence: Q2 2026 sales grew 13% reported and 4.8% on a comparable basis; GAAP EPS was $0.53 versus adjusted $1.31.
ABT.risk: Product and reimbursement risk; acquisition and adjustment effects complicate growth comparisons.
ABT.reviewGate: Review organic growth, GAAP-to-adjusted reconciliation and device competition.

ISRG.name: Intuitive Surgical
ISRG.fit: Robotic surgery adds procedure-driven medical-technology exposure.
ISRG.evidence: Q2 2026 worldwide da Vinci and Ion procedures grew about 16%; installed da Vinci systems grew 12%.
ISRG.risk: Hospital budgets, competing systems, reimbursement and valuation risk.
ISRG.reviewGate: Assess recurring instruments revenue and procedure economics against the price paid.

PL.name: Planet Labs
PL.fit: Earth-observation data adds a commercial space-data business.
PL.evidence: September 2026 company announcements include a German dedicated-constellation contract and a European defence/intelligence agreement.
PL.risk: Government/customer concentration, satellite replacement spending and dilution.
PL.reviewGate: Read Q2 FY2027 cash flow and contract terms; distinguish backlog from recognised revenue. Already present in the Alphabet basket.

HII.name: Huntington Ingalls Industries
HII.fit: Naval shipbuilding diversifies an aerospace-heavy defence basket.
HII.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue rose 10.9% to $3.4bn; operating margin was 6.1%.
HII.risk: Fixed-price contracts, labour constraints and concentrated government customers.
HII.reviewGate: Check programme-level execution and cash flow; avoid valuing backlog as guaranteed profit.

AVAV.name: AeroVironment
AVAV.fit: Autonomous systems and space/cyber technologies provide a different defence mix.
AVAV.evidence: FY2027 Q1 revenue grew 6% to $480.5m; funded backlog was $1.5bn, up 37%.
AVAV.risk: Acquisition accounting, contract timing and spending concentration; speculative relative to mature defence primes.
AVAV.reviewGate: Reconcile organic growth, intangible amortisation and free cash flow; evaluate funded rather than total pipeline.

CME.name: CME Group
CME.fit: Regulated crypto derivatives infrastructure is an indirect blockchain exposure.
CME.evidence: Q2 2026 crypto average daily volume grew 32% to 250,000 contracts; the overall company reported $1.7bn revenue.
CME.risk: Crypto is only one business line; exchange competition and regulation matter.
CME.reviewGate: Quantify crypto contribution; do not treat the stock as equivalent to owning cryptocurrency. Already in Alphabet.

IBKR.name: Interactive Brokers Group
IBKR.fit: Brokerage distribution and custody access provide indirect digital-asset infrastructure exposure.
IBKR.evidence: July 2026 announcement expanded supported crypto tokens and stablecoin withdrawal capabilities.
IBKR.risk: Most earnings are from the wider brokerage business; rates, trading activity and operational risk dominate.
IBKR.reviewGate: Measure materiality of crypto economics and rate sensitivity rather than assigning a crypto multiple.

NU.name: Nu Holdings
NU.fit: Digital banking expands payments exposure to Latin America.
NU.evidence: Q2 2026 company release reported 139m customers and quarterly net income above $1bn.
NU.risk: Consumer-credit losses, currencies and country regulation; this is a lender, not simply a payments network.
NU.reviewGate: Examine delinquency vintages, cost of risk, capital and customer profitability.

MELI.name: MercadoLibre
MELI.fit: Mercado Pago combines payments with a commerce distribution network.
MELI.evidence: Q2 2026 payment volume reached $101bn, up 56%; operating income declined 17% despite strong revenue growth.
MELI.risk: Credit exposure, Latin American currencies, competition and reinvestment pressure on margins.
MELI.reviewGate: Separate commerce, payments and lending economics; assess credit quality and sustainable margins.

BWA.name: BorgWarner
BWA.fit: Propulsion components diversify exposure beyond EV manufacturers.
BWA.evidence: Q2 2026 sales rose 0.3% reported but fell 1.2% organically; battery-energy sales declined about $60m.
BWA.risk: EV adoption delays and legacy combustion exposure; not a pure EV business.
BWA.reviewGate: Require a segment-level EV growth case rather than treating total sales as EV revenue.

STM.name: STMicroelectronics
STM.fit: Automotive and power semiconductors complement automakers and battery suppliers.
STM.evidence: Q2 2026 reported operating margin was 5.4%, net income $222m and net financial position $2.01bn.
STM.risk: Auto/industrial inventory cycles, capital intensity and silicon-carbide competition.
STM.reviewGate: Validate automotive and EV revenue mix and utilisation; do not use company-wide AI growth as EV evidence.

TLN.name: Talen Energy
TLN.fit: Existing nuclear generation adds operating-asset exposure alongside reactor developers.
TLN.evidence: Company reported 2.2GW nuclear capacity within approximately 15.6GW total capacity; Q2 GAAP loss was $92m versus adjusted EBITDA $374m.
TLN.risk: Significant fossil fleet, power prices, nuclear outages and leverage; not a pure nuclear company.
TLN.reviewGate: Reconcile hedging-related accounting, debt and cash flow; examine power-contract concentration.

SPGI.name: S&P Global
SPGI.fit: Ratings, indices and data support a potential recurring-revenue and embedded-workflow moat.
SPGI.evidence: Q2 2026 GAAP revenue rose 10% to $4.146bn; Mobility was spun off on July 1, requiring comparable-base adjustments.
SPGI.risk: Debt-issuance cycles, regulation, AI/data competition and valuation.
SPGI.reviewGate: Compare post-spin earnings, retention and return on capital; do not compare unadjusted historical multiples.

MCO.name: Moody’s
MCO.fit: Ratings and risk analytics diversify a consumer/technology-heavy moat basket.
MCO.risk: Debt issuance cyclicality, regulation and overlap with S&P Global.
MCO.reviewGate: Compare recurring analytics growth and through-cycle earnings; consider one rather than both ratings companies. Already in Berkshire.

CB.name: Chubb
CB.fit: Filing-backed candidate for the Berkshire strategy.
CB.evidence: Berkshire reported 34,249,183 shares at June 30, 2026, absent from our copied basket.
CB.risk: Ownership is lagged and does not disclose the purchase thesis; insurance catastrophe and reserving risks remain.
CB.reviewGate: Check subsequent filings and insurer valuation; do not copy the reported dollar weight into AGI automatically.

BRK.B.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B
BRK.B.fit: Filing-backed candidate for the Gates strategy.
BRK.B.evidence: Gates Trust reported 14,689,844 Class B shares at June 30, 2026.
BRK.B.risk: Look-through overlap with the separate Berkshire basket; quarter-end ownership may have changed.
BRK.B.reviewGate: Verify the Class B instrument and current filings; assess underlying business and holding overlap.

CNI.name: Canadian National Railway
CNI.fit: Filing-backed candidate for the Gates strategy.
CNI.evidence: Gates Trust reported 51,826,786 shares at June 30, 2026.
CNI.risk: Rail volume cycles, labour disruption, capital spending and CAD exposure.
CNI.reviewGate: Verify current ownership and operating/cash returns; filing ownership alone is not a valuation thesis.

FIG.name: Figma
FIG.fit: Filing-backed candidate for the Alphabet strategy; product design software exposure.
FIG.evidence: Alphabet reported 215,582 shares at June 30, 2026; Figma Q2 revenue grew 48% to $370.1m.
FIG.risk: Small disclosed stake is not an endorsement; AI competition and stock compensation matter.
FIG.reviewGate: Check subsequent ownership, dilution and durable software economics before considering a weight.

BEAM.name: Beam Therapeutics
BEAM.fit: Filing-backed candidate for Alphabet; precision genetic medicines.
BEAM.evidence: Alphabet reported 321,604 shares at June 30, 2026. Beam describes clinical base-editing programmes.
BEAM.risk: Speculative clinical, regulatory and financing risk.
BEAM.reviewGate: Review trial endpoints, cash runway and next catalysts; do not infer success from Alphabet ownership.

IMTM.name: iShares MSCI Intl Momentum Factor ETF
IMTM.fit: International momentum complements the existing US factor sleeves.
IMTM.evidence: Tracks developed-market stocks outside the US with stronger price momentum; disclosed expense ratio 0.30%.
IMTM.risk: Momentum reversals, turnover, currency exposure and overlap with international holdings.
IMTM.reviewGate: Compare combined factor exposures and turnover, not just the number of ETF names.

IQLT.name: iShares MSCI Intl Quality Factor ETF
IQLT.fit: International quality broadens the factor framework.
IQLT.evidence: Issuer identifies this as the international quality factor ETF.
IQLT.risk: Equity and currency risk; quality can be expensive and overlap with other developed-market funds.
IQLT.reviewGate: Read current holdings and methodology; measure combined country/sector weights before sizing.

AVUV.name: Avantis U.S. Small Cap Value ETF
AVUV.fit: Adds a small-cap value/profitability sleeve missing from a large-cap-led allocation.
AVUV.evidence: Actively managed US small-cap value ETF; issuer expense ratio 0.25%.
AVUV.risk: Smaller-company volatility, liquidity and prolonged factor underperformance.
AVUV.reviewGate: Treat as a replacement for part of US equity allocation, not extra risk outside the target equity budget.

IEMG.name: iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF
IEMG.fit: Alternative implementation of the existing emerging-market allocation.
IEMG.evidence: Tracks large-, mid- and small-cap emerging-market equities; issuer expense ratio 0.09%.
IEMG.risk: Country, currency and geopolitical concentration; overlaps EEM.
IEMG.reviewGate: Compare with EEM and replace if justified; holding both is not a new asset class.

VGIT.name: Vanguard Intermediate-Term Treasury ETF
VGIT.fit: A dedicated Treasury sleeve separates duration exposure from corporate credit.
VGIT.evidence: Vanguard lists the intermediate-term government bond ETF with a 0.03% expense ratio.
VGIT.risk: Interest-rate duration can produce losses; USD exposure remains for Indian clients.
VGIT.reviewGate: Check total duration and reduce another bond allocation rather than exceeding the portfolio budget.

VTIP.name: Vanguard Short-Term Inflation-Protected Securities ETF
VTIP.fit: Short-duration US inflation-linked bonds add a distinct inflation sleeve.
VTIP.evidence: Vanguard identifies VTIP as its short-term inflation-protected securities ETF.
VTIP.risk: Protects against US inflation, not Indian inflation or currency loss; real yields can rise.
VTIP.reviewGate: Compare duration and real yield; decide whether this replaces nominal bonds or longer TIPS.

USFR.name: WisdomTree Floating Rate Treasury Fund
USFR.fit: Alternative to part of the existing short-term Treasury/cash sleeve.
USFR.evidence: Holds US Treasury floating-rate notes; issuer expense ratio 0.15%.
USFR.risk: Income falls with short-term rates; not an insured bank deposit or an INR capital guarantee.
USFR.reviewGate: Compare net yield and dealing costs with SGOV; avoid treating two cash ETFs as diversification.

VGSH.name: Vanguard Short-Term Treasury ETF
VGSH.fit: Short nominal Treasuries are a conservative bond-sleeve alternative.
VGSH.evidence: Vanguard identifies VGSH as its short-term Treasury ETF.
VGSH.risk: Some duration risk and USD/INR risk; reinvestment yields can decline.
VGSH.reviewGate: Compare maturity exposure with SGOV and USFR and choose the intended role.

SCHH.name: Schwab U.S. REIT ETF
SCHH.fit: Alternative implementation of Swensen’s real-estate sleeve.
SCHH.evidence: Issuer lists a US REIT ETF with a 0.07% expense ratio.
SCHH.risk: Real-estate sector and rate sensitivity; overlaps VNQ but does not have identical coverage.
SCHH.reviewGate: Compare index coverage and costs as a VNQ replacement, not an extra real-estate allocation.

SCHF.name: Schwab International Equity ETF
SCHF.fit: Alternative implementation of Swensen’s developed-market equity sleeve.
SCHF.evidence: Issuer lists an international equity ETF with a 0.03% expense ratio.
SCHF.risk: Foreign equity/currency risk and overlapping holdings; benchmark coverage differs from VEA.
SCHF.reviewGate: Compare country and small-cap coverage before substituting for VEA.

DBMF.name: iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF
DBMF.fit: Potential diversifier for an explicitly modified All Weather portfolio.
DBMF.evidence: Issuer describes replication of leading managed-futures strategies using liquid futures exposures.
DBMF.risk: Trend reversals, model risk, derivatives and fees; protection in every downturn is not guaranteed.
DBMF.reviewGate: Requires a separately named AGI variant and a correlation/drawdown study; not part of the existing reference recipe.

genomics.name: Genomics
genomics.note: Tools diversify the genomics value chain; PACB is a speculative watchlist candidate.

cybersecurity.name: Cybersecurity
cybersecurity.note: Cloud/network security and application security extend the security workloads covered.

artificial-intelligence.name: Artificial Intelligence
artificial-intelligence.note: Networking and power/cooling broaden exposure beyond chips and software; common AI-spending risk remains.

us-top10.name: US Top10
us-top10.note: No names qualify automatically. The copied snapshot discloses only 3 holdings/29.6%. Obtain the remaining seven and the momentum rules before claiming an addition. A separately defined AGI S&P 100 momentum screen would be a new strategy.

cloud-computing.name: Cloud Computing
cloud-computing.note: Enterprise cloud infrastructure and physical interconnection add different business models.

big-tech.name: Big Tech
big-tech.note: Large infrastructure platforms fit; exposure overlaps the AI and cloud portfolios.

alphabet-strategy.name: Alphabet Strategy
alphabet-strategy.note: Both names appear in the June 30, 2026 Alphabet 13F. These are candidates for an expanded AGI filing-based variant, not claims that Vested holds them today.

blackrock-smart-beta.name: BlackRock Smart Beta
blackrock-smart-beta.note: Extend factors outside the US while retaining an ETF-based implementation.

deglobalization.name: Deglobalization
deglobalization.note: Grid building and automation are plausible beneficiaries; revenue geography must support the thesis.

critical-minerals.name: Critical Minerals
critical-minerals.note: Diversified miners provide scale, but iron ore can dilute critical-minerals exposure.

clean-energy.name: Clean Energy
clean-energy.note: These fit a broad electrification portfolio. They should not be presented as pure renewable-energy holdings.

aging.name: Aging
aging.note: Diagnostics, devices and surgical procedures broaden healthcare exposure.

space-tech.name: Space Tech
space-tech.note: One additional candidate rather than padding the list. Iridium was reviewed but deferred because its reported Rocket Lab acquisition introduces deal risk and overlap.

berkshire-strategy.name: Berkshire Strategy
berkshire-strategy.note: Only a filing-backed candidate here; do not invent additional Berkshire holdings or manager rationale.

global-multi-asset-aggressive.name: Global Multi-Asset (Aggressive)
global-multi-asset-aggressive.note: AVUV adds a factor sleeve; IEMG is an alternative to EEM. Rebalance within existing asset-class budgets.

gates-strategy.name: Gates Strategy
gates-strategy.note: Both appear in the June 30, 2026 Trust filing and are absent from our copied basket. The filing is not a live holdings feed.

swensen-portfolio.name: Swensen Portfolio
swensen-portfolio.note: These are substitute funds for existing asset-class sleeves, not reasons to increase equity/REIT weights.

moat.name: Moat
moat.note: Ratings/data infrastructure is a useful research direction. Both together create industry concentration; a moat does not establish a cheap price.

global-multi-asset-moderate.name: Global Multi-Asset (Moderate)
global-multi-asset-moderate.note: Separate credit, nominal duration and inflation exposure before deciding target weights.

all-weather.name: All Weather
all-weather.note: Adding these changes the reference recipe; publish as a distinct AGI variant only after testing.

defense-security.name: Defense & Security
defense-security.note: Naval shipbuilding and autonomous systems diversify the types of defence contracts.

global-multi-asset-conservative.name: Global Multi-Asset (Conservative)
global-multi-asset-conservative.note: Alternatives within the bond/cash allocation. Existing SGOV already provides similar capital-stability intent.

blockchain-ecosystem.name: Blockchain Ecosystem
blockchain-ecosystem.note: Indirect infrastructure exposure is less crypto-pure; it is not equivalent to holding tokens.

digital-cash.name: Digital Cash
digital-cash.note: Latin American digital finance broadens geography but introduces lending and currency risks.

electric-vehicles.name: Electric Vehicles
electric-vehicles.note: Component suppliers broaden the value chain, but EV-specific revenue must be measured.

nuclear-energy.name: Nuclear Energy
nuclear-energy.note: Operating nuclear generation and reactor technology complement uranium/development holdings; both are diversified businesses.

deferred.reason: Reported pending acquisition by Rocket Lab, already in the Space portfolio. Deal-dependent exposure is not the intended diversification.
